requirements.title: Processors may support gradual or abrupt underflow mode control with performance latitude
requirements.source: S17.5 p1; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF483.
requirements.definition: Some processors allow execution-time control over gradual underflow, producing subnormal numbers, versus abrupt underflow, producing zero; abrupt mode may improve performance.

pending.underflow-mode-control-processor-depende: No portable oracle requires underflow-mode control; fixtures first query IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL and skip control effects on the false branch.
pending.gradual-underflow-produces-subnormal: Guard probe: kind X has IEEE_SUPPORT_DATATYPE(X) true for the IEEE_CLASS observer, IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL(X) true, IEEE_SUPPORT_SUBNORMAL(X) true, and IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(IEEE_UNDERFLOW,X) true. Apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(IEEE_UNDERFLOW,X). TRUE branch: set gradual mode, compute TINY(X)/2.0_X, and assert IEEE_CLASS reports a positive subnormal result. FALSE branch: skip.
pending.abrupt-underflow-produces-zero: Guard probe: kind X supports underflow control and abrupt mode. TRUE branch: set abrupt mode, compute TINY(X)/2.0_X through volatile variables, assert result is zero and restore saved mode. FALSE branch: skip.
pending.abrupt-underflow-performance-latitude: No portable oracle constrains performance; fixtures must not compare timings between gradual and abrupt modes.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. IEEE effects are tested only under explicit capability probes; the TRUE branch asserts the concrete flag, mode, type, constant, or operation effect, and the FALSE branch is a skip rather than a pass. Named FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE(flag,x): under IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG(flag,x), if IEEE_SUPPORT_HALTING(flag) then CALL IEEE_SET_HALTING_MODE(flag,.FALSE.); else CALL IEEE_GET_HALTING_MODE(flag,h) and proceed only if h is .FALSE. (otherwise skip); CALL IEEE_SET_FLAG(IEEE_ALL,.FALSE.). Positive plans establish a non-default state first by setting distinguished sentinel values and apply FLAG-ROW-PREAMBLE before any exception operation or flag-state assertion unless the row explicitly says the preamble is not applied because it would destroy the initial-state oracle.

requirements.title: IEEE underflow mode procedures inquire, set, and restore supported modes
requirements.source: S17.5 p2.control-procedures, p2.initial-latitude, p2.procedure-restore; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF483.
requirements.definition: IEEE_SET_UNDERFLOW_MODE controls underflow mode, IEEE_GET_UNDERFLOW_MODE gets it, IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL inquires support, the initial mode is processor dependent, and procedures other than IEEE_SET_UNDERFLOW_MODE or IEEE_SET_STATUS preserve and restore the mode.

pending.ieee-support-underflow-control-inquires-: Guard probe: compile USE, INTRINSIC :: IEEE_ARITHMETIC, ONLY: IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL. TRUE branch: call with default real into a logical sentinel and branch on the result; no support result is forced. FALSE branch: skip.
pending.ieee-get-underflow-mode-retrieves-curren: Guard probe: IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL(X) true. TRUE branch: set mode .true., initialize result .false., GET observes .true.; set .false., initialize result .true., GET observes .false.; restore saved mode. FALSE branch: skip.
pending.ieee-set-underflow-mode-alters-current-m: Guard probe: same support. TRUE branch: SET to the opposite of saved mode and GET observes the opposite before restoration. FALSE branch: skip.
pending.initial-underflow-mode-processor-depende: No portable oracle fixes the initial underflow mode; fixtures save it at start and restore it at completion.
pending.underflow-mode-unchanged-on-procedure-en: Guard probe: support true; caller sets saved mode to .true. then calls helper. TRUE branch: helper first GET observes .true. before setters. FALSE branch: skip.
pending.underflow-mode-restored-on-procedure-ret: Guard probe: same helper changes mode to .false., calls IEEE_GET_UNDERFLOW_MODE before return, and confirms .false. was the changed in-helper value. TRUE branch: caller GET observes original .true. after return, then restores the process initial mode. FALSE branch: skip.

requirements.title: Underflow mode affects only types whose support inquiry is true
requirements.source: S17.5 p3; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF483.
requirements.definition: Underflow mode affects only floating-point calculations of a type corresponding to an X for which IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL returns true.

pending.underflow-mode-effects-guarded-by-suppor: Guard probe: for each profiled real kind X, IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL(X) returns true. TRUE branch: run the gradual versus abrupt TINY(X)/2.0_X oracle for that kind only. FALSE branch: skip effect assertions for that kind.
pending.underflow-mode-no-effect-assertion-for-s: Guard probe: IEEE_SUPPORT_UNDERFLOW_CONTROL(Y) returns false for a profiled kind Y. TRUE branch: set/get underflow mode using a supported kind elsewhere, then perform tiny calculations of kind Y only as a smoke run; no value difference is asserted. FALSE branch: skip.

accounting.rationale: Underflow-mode control and performance are processor-dependent permissions, with gradual/abrupt meanings recorded.
Control procedures, initial latitude, and procedure restore are split.
Initial underflow mode is processor dependent.
Underflow mode affects only calculations for supported types.

review_rationale: Source registration for the Clause 17 heading and 17.1-17.5: the IEEE overview, derived types and constants, exceptions, rounding modes and underflow mode (batch213). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across four rounds; every flag row uses a named halting-off preamble and every mode round trip observes the changed value before restoring. Source accounting only.
